situation:
You are the operations manager for REDBIRD FRY HOUSE, a two-year-old fried chicken franchise with nine stores. The founder (judge) opened the first store on money raised in a single funding round, and what is left of that round now covers about seven months of operating cash.

Utilities have become the third-largest cost line in every store. The fryer bank and the hood exhaust run from open to close, and the dining rooms stay lit and cooled through the last three hours of the night, when nearly every order arrives at the drive-thru window instead.

The local utility has filed for a rate increase that the state regulator has not approved. A high-efficiency fryer and hood-control package would cut energy use enough to pay for itself in under two years if that increase takes effect, and would return almost nothing if it is denied. Buying the package now spends roughly a third of the cash the company has left.

The other course is to close the dining rooms at eight and run the drive-thru only for the last three hours, holding less breaded chicken in the warmer through a slow evening. Cash is saved immediately, but evening guests would reach a locked door the tagline "Fried Fresh 'Til Close" told them would be open, and the closing crew would count the night deposit with fewer people on the floor.

The founder (judge) has asked you to recommend one of the two courses, to explain how the closing crew should describe the change to guests who ask about it, and to propose a tagline that would still be true afterward. The founder (judge) will greet you, hear your ideas and ask questions, and will thank you when the presentation is over.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the founder (judge) of REDBIRD FRY HOUSE. Business background is the same as the situation above. Nine stores are open, about seven months of operating cash remains, utilities are the third-largest cost line, and the utility's proposed rate increase is still sitting with the state regulator.

You want the operations manager to recommend either buying the high-efficiency fryer and hood-control package now or closing the dining rooms at eight and running the drive-thru only, to tell you how the closing crew should explain the change to guests, and to offer a tagline that would still be true.

During the presentation you are to ask the following questions of each participant:
judgeQuestions: A year from now, how would we know this was the right call?
What would tell us early that it is not working?
